red.focus: Learn to find an operative rule rather than repeat a case's story.
red.summary: A court decision contains facts, arguments, and reasons, but not every sentence states a binding rule. Learn to identify the legal question decided, the outcome, and why the court reached it.
checklist: I can name the question a judgment decided
I can distinguish what a court held from surrounding commentary
I can state a narrow rule tied to the facts

sections.title: A judgment solves a particular dispute
sections.body_md: A customer sues a manufacturer after a sealed drink allegedly contains a dangerous object. A legal report discusses the parties, the claimed harm, and reasons a manufacturer might owe care to a consumer without a contract. The report may also include comments about social responsibility. A reader who copies every line as a rule will mislead the client. First ask what question the court had authority to answer. In Donoghue v Stevenson, the central question concerned a possible duty of care; the House of Lords did not finally prove the alleged snail or determine every element of damages.

sections.title: Separate holding from explanation
sections.body_md: A holding is the legal conclusion required to decide the issue presented in the case. Supporting reasoning can explain its scope; broader observations may be dicta rather than controlling propositions in a precedent-based system. Courts and legal systems differ in how such distinctions operate. The beginner should record the material facts, legal issue, disposition, and essential reasoning. Do not quote a broad phrase as permission for any lawsuit. A precedent about contaminated products does not, by itself, establish liability for an unrelated employment dispute.

sections.title: Write a rule with conditions
sections.body_md: A helpful first rule statement is: In the relevant common-law setting, a manufacturer may owe reasonable care to an ultimate consumer of a product intended to reach them without an effective intervening inspection. Then identify limits and what still must be proved. The word may matters: a duty does not mean negligence, causation, and loss have been established. Good extraction makes a case easier to apply and harder to exaggerate. Compare your statement to the actual reasons in the opinion, and mark uncertainties for further research.

yellow.focus: Produce precise case briefs and identify ratio decidendi across different fact patterns.
yellow.summary: Legal rules come from operative text and authoritative interpretations, not isolated quotations. Distinguish a case's ratio, factual limits, procedural posture, and later treatment before applying it.
checklist: I can create a five-part case brief using real sources
I can test whether factual differences are material
I can record negative and subsequent treatment of authority

sections.title: Build a compact brief
sections.body_md: Brief a judgment using five fields: relevant facts, legal issue, decision, essential legal reasoning, and disposition. Add the court's place in the hierarchy and the date. Suppose a court finds an official search unlawful because no statute or common-law rule authorized the interference. The rule should concern absence of lawful power, not the entire biography of the person searched. Note whether the case was an appeal, preliminary question, or merits decision; procedural posture affects what was actually decided. Clear briefs allow another reader to check the source quickly.

The rule should concern absence of lawful power, not the entire biography of the person searched. Note whether the case was an appeal, preliminary question, or merits decision; procedural posture affects what was actually decided. Clear briefs allow another reader to check the source quickly.

sections.title: Ratio depends on what mattered
sections.body_md: A court describes several facts, but only some support the rule necessary for the outcome. If the decision involved a government search of a private home, a later case involving a voluntary consensual inspection may be distinguishable. The lawyer must explain why consent changes the legal question rather than merely assert that the cases look different. Ratio decidendi is a familiar concept in many common-law systems, yet formulations and binding effects vary. It should not be imposed unchanged on civil-law judgments that use a different precedent structure.

sections.title: Check the case's continuing status
sections.body_md: A reported case may have been reversed, distinguished, limited, or overtaken by legislation. Extracting a beautiful rule from a superseded authority can damage the client's case. Use reliable citators and the relevant current statute where available, and identify whether adverse authority is binding. In a research log, distinguish the historical rule a case announced from the law now controlling the facts. A good case brief is a starting point for verification, not a substitute for it.

orange.focus: Extract rules from complex statutes and multi-opinion judgments.
orange.summary: Not every case has one uncontested rationale, and not every statutory rule exists in a single sentence. Develop a source-first method for synthesizing multiple opinions, defined terms, exceptions, and temporal amendments.
checklist: I can distinguish a judgment from separate judicial reasons
I can identify statutory definitions, conditions and exceptions
I can avoid claiming a single majority rationale without support

sections.title: Agreement in result need not equal agreement in reasons
sections.body_md: An appellate court may reach a majority disposition through opinions that disagree on the necessary rationale. Counting which judges joined which propositions is essential before describing a passage as the holding of the court. In U.S. Supreme Court plurality settings, Marks v United States proposes a narrowest-grounds method where applicable, but identifying a common rationale can be contested. Do not mechanically label the shortest opinion binding or assume the doctrine transfers to every legal order. Build a vote and reasoning map before announcing the governing proposition.

Do not mechanically label the shortest opinion binding or assume the doctrine transfers to every legal order. Build a vote and reasoning map before announcing the governing proposition.

sections.title: A statute's conditions may be dispersed
sections.body_md: A consumer rights statute might state a general remedy in one section, define a protected consumer elsewhere, and create exceptions in schedules. Extracting only the remedy sentence would omit who qualifies and when proceedings must start. Locate definitions, cross-references, transitional provisions, and any controlling regulations. Check the version effective at the relevant date. A compact rule should use conditional structure: if specified persons and facts satisfy the conditions, the authority permits or requires a specified consequence, unless an applicable exception or defense changes it.

sections.title: Synthesize without erasing disagreement
sections.body_md: Suppose two lines of appellate authority describe when an agency may exercise discretion. One emphasizes statutory text; another applies a particular reasonableness framework. Check whether they govern different categories, were decided under amended law, or actually conflict. State the hierarchy and any unresolved tension. A master's synthesis must show the reader which source supports each proposition and where the gap remains. It should not invent a harmonizing rule for the sake of a clean outline. When authority is unsettled, uncertainty belongs in the answer, followed by the strongest legally supportable interpretation.

black.focus: Construct a jurisprudentially sound rule-extraction protocol for contested authority.
black.summary: Extracting law is an interpretive act shaped by institutional sources, precedent, and contested theories of judicial authority. Build an auditable model that distinguishes legal validity, interpretive choice, and normative evaluation.
checklist: I can compare source-based and principled approaches to legal rule identification
I can audit a complex authority chain for conflict and change
I can state candid legal uncertainty without surrendering analysis

sections.title: An algorithm cannot settle every legal disagreement
sections.body_md: A software tool may identify repeated phrases in judgments and rank them by citation count, yet binding doctrine depends on who decided what, procedural posture, subsequent authority, and legally relevant facts. A frequency count is not a rule of recognition. Hartian accounts attend to social sources of law, while interpretivists dispute whether principles fitting and justifying practice are reducible to an inventory of sources. A doctoral protocol should state its theory of authority openly. It must not treat an extracted sentence as self-authenticating law.

sections.title: Trace propositions to institutional authority
sections.body_md: Take a contested constitutional claim and record a provenance graph: enacted provision, original cases, conflicting interpretations, controlling later rulings, and exceptions. Identify the actual decision maker and whether the asserted ratio was necessary to the result. Explain tensions among text, purpose, precedent, and jurisdictional competence rather than hiding them in a polished summary. The method should allow later researchers to reproduce each step, distinguish an authoritative proposition from a persuasive one, and update a conclusion when new binding authority appears.

sections.title: Preserve uncertainty as a professional obligation
sections.body_md: When authority supports two plausible interpretations, counsel should evaluate comparative strength, litigation consequences, and the client's choices, not declare that ambiguity eliminates a duty of competence. Do not fabricate a consensus or conceal a directly adverse controlling authority. State what a court would have to decide, why one reading is stronger, and what change in facts or law could reverse the conclusion. The final rule extraction should be concise enough to use yet transparent enough to challenge. Legal scholarship serves persons affected by decisions, not an illusion of perfect certainty.
